design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (grooming_appointment_care, category groom).
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 5]}. Tree = root + 1 prerequisite; the pass late-cancellation fee takes 6 factors, the pass refund takes 5. Draw for task 1 (headroom check, --tasks 2): 1 prerequisite, factor_counts [6, 4].
[Scope snapshot] Occupied before this task: nothing. Claimed here: groom_ext_pass_late_cancel_fee (agent, charge_late_cancel_fee_38a40f67) and groom_ext_pass_cancel_refund (customer, cancel_groom_pass_241c8b1d), i.e. the prepaid-pass side of groom_cancellation_no_show and groom_pass_cancel_refund. Reserved headroom for task 1: the Groom Club Monthly side of the same two base policies (club late-cancellation charge + club cancellation settlement), which have different value bases (one club visit, the early termination fee) and a different customer-owned tool. Headroom finding recorded honestly: the only customer-owned writes in the blueprint that carry a number are the two cancellations (prepaid refund, club settlement); visit checkouts, purchases and club billing all trigger member points and may not be written, so each task's tree is built around one cancellation plus the late-cancellation booking that the cancellation's settlement waits on. Base mapping parameters (single_visit_price_by_size_usd, pass_price_by_size_usd) cannot be indexed by the restricted compute grammar, so the refund baseline uses the per-visit paid rate (price_paid_usd / visits_purchased) and declares the override of the base valuation sentence.
[Why a good test] Surface goal: 'cancel Juniper's grooming pass and get back whatever money is left'. The scored value (refund_usd) is hidden behind (1) a prerequisite the customer never mentions: the refund rule says 'The refund on a cancelled pass is fixed only after every cancellation on the pass that is recorded with a fee remedy carries its late-cancellation fee entry.' and the pass history shows the 2026-10-02 cancellation (remedy fee) with no fee entry; the only write that books that entry is the pass late-cancellation fee policy's write; (2) a 6-factor fee computation over the cancelled booking, the weekday, the notice, a 6-month missed-booking window, the Tailwise Plus tier (member) and the pet's wellness plan office visits (vet); (3) a 5-factor refund over the used-visit ledger, the discount and validity span, days to expiry, the redo count, Autoship shipments (autoship) and the fee just booked. Depth: surface goal -> refund rule -> prerequisite state -> fee policy -> fee write -> refund. Breadth: 4 categories read (groom, member, vet, autoship), 3 history windows (6-month missed bookings, 6-month Autoship shipments, lifetime used visits/redos), date spans (weekday, days to expiry, months since purchase).
[Problem-tree card] root groom_ext_pass_cancel_refund (owner=user tool cancel_groom_pass_241c8b1d) <- groom_ext_pass_late_cancel_fee (owner=agent tool charge_late_cancel_fee_38a40f67). Edge kind value_input, gate fees_booked, form state, policy_source = the sentence quoted above (four-point test: ordering connective 'only after'; record-visible state 'cancellation recorded with a fee remedy carries its late-cancellation fee entry', named in the words of the history finder; no tool, id or snake_case token; strength 'only after', scope 'every cancellation on the pass that is recorded with a fee remedy' = the condition). Exactly one write of this difficulty books a late-cancellation fee entry on a prepaid pass: the pass fee policy's write (the club policy books a club late-cancellation charge entry on a club). Derivation: sentence + history (e13 remedy fee, no fee row) + fee rule ('booked to the pass as a late-cancellation fee entry for the cancelled booking') -> book the pass late-cancellation fee first. Seed evidence of falsity: groom_events e13.late_cancel_remedy = fee, original_event_id = e12, no groom_late_cancel_fee row. Topological order: fee (step 10) then refund (step 14). Deletion sensitivity (run): skipping step 10 gives refund 115.67 instead of 112.81 and leaves no fee row. user_scenario never mentions a fee or charge; tools validate nothing.
[Base-invariant card] Fee write (subject groom_late_cancel_fee): governing base policy groom_cancellation_no_show; its only gate free_cancel_notice applies to groom_appointment_cancel, not to the fee write, so the write is policy_scope; the late remedy is already recorded on e13 (notice 15 < 24, Full Groom late_cancel_forfeits_visit false -> fee); the clause 'A late cancellation carries late_cancel_fee_usd, or, where late_cancel_forfeits_visit is true, forfeits one visit instead of the fee' is overridden for prepaid passes by the computed fee (declared in overwrite); 'A fee or forfeit is never charged twice for the same booking' holds (no fee row for e12). Refund write (subjects groom_pass_cancel, groom_pass_refund): governing base groom_pass_cancel_refund; its time gate full_refund_window (anchor purchased_on, calendar days, day 0, inclusive, 14 days) is retired by the declared overwrite that restates it as the full-refund branch of the extended rule; at frozen_time DAYS(2025-11-20, 2026-10-05) = 319 > 14 and 4 visits are used, so the full branch is false (just-short case: a request on 2025-12-04 with no visit used would be refunded in full; 2025-12-05 would not). Pass status active (allowed for cancellation), only the customer cancels (user tool).
[Business-object card] Target object: pass P0 (Full Groom Pass 6-Visit, Juniper). Fee: correlation key original_event_id = e12 (the booking) via cancellation e13; excluded: e11 (free cancellation, remedy none), e10/e8/e5/e3/e1 bookings. Refund aggregates: used visits = e2, e6 (completed) + e4, e9 (no-shows with visits_delta 1); redo e7 (of visit e6); fee rows = the step-10 row; Pistachio's pass P1 is never aggregated (different groom_pass_id). The refund row written by the tool carries groom_pass_id P0.
[Factor card: fee] addon_part: booked deshed_treatment -> 12.50 (baseline 0, result 3.52). slot_multiplier: Saturday -> 1.25 (baseline 1, 4.57). notice_treatment (method): 15 h >= 12 -> proration 9/24 (baseline whole basis, 15.23). repeat_multiplier: 2 missed in 6 months -> 1.5 (baseline 1, 3.81); near-miss e4 no-show 2026-03-14 is 6 whole months back and the free cancellation e11 is not a missed booking. plus_relief (cross member): Tailwise Plus Annual active -> 25% (baseline 0, 11.43). clinic_relief (cross-category vet read, not a difficulty; multi-source: plan active AND gap): office visit 2026-09-24, 9 days before -> 50% (baseline 0, 17.14); near-miss telehealth 2026-10-02 (1 day before) is not an office visit and would wrongly give the 100% waiver. Fall-back with every baseline: 20.00. Gold 5.71.
[Factor card: refund] used_visit_value (method): multi_pet + 10 months >= 6 -> latest used visit undiscounted (baseline 118.17). expiry_share: 46 days -> 0.75 (143.16). redo_credit: one redo -> 32.13 (80.68). autoship_admin_fee (cross autoship): 3 charged shipments in 6 months -> 7.50 (105.31); near-misses: 2026-03-28 charge (6 months back) and the 2026-08-01 skip. fee_withholding_share: one fee entry -> 50% (109.96). Fall-back 107.81. Gold 112.81. No stamp decides any tier: discount_kind is the purchase record of the discount actually applied, the tier also needs the elapsed months; the pass's visits_remaining cache agrees with the ledger (2).
[Seed rows] customer/pets/store/passes/member/vet/autoship rows exist because a read node consumes each: removing e9 drops the repeat multiplier to 1 and changes the used count; removing ve2 removes the clinic relief; removing ae3/ae4/ae6 drops the admin tier; removing e7 removes the redo credit; removing e13 removes the fee obligation and the prerequisite. Automatic clauses: no pass expires before frozen_time (P0 expires 2026-11-20; P1 already exhausted), no club billing, no open booking remains, Autoship next ship 2026-10-24, vet next payment 2026-10-10: nothing new falls due at frozen_time other than the fee.
[Persona] Delphine, tired and polite; volunteers only the goal and the vet-advised reason; gives phone then card last four only when asked; mentions the Saturday app cancellation only if asked about appointments; agrees to 'some charge' only after the agent explains it; refuses extension/transfer; runs the hand-over with the agent's figure; closes when told the pass is cancelled and the refund is going back. No ask of her own beyond the cancellation.
[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, card) -> passes -> P0 history (find the fee-remedy cancellation without a fee entry) -> pets -> store -> membership -> vet plan -> plan ledger -> unlock+call fee 5.71 for booking e12 -> Autoship subscriptions and ledger -> unlock user tool -> customer calls cancel_groom_pass_241c8b1d(P0, 112.81).
[Verification run] Authoring recompute (check_compute primitives on the handling-time world) printed fee trace fee_basis 40.625, after_notice 15.234375, missed 2, after_repeat 22.8515625, relief 75 -> 5.71; refund trace used 4, used_value 264.18, unused 121.38, days_left 46, redo 32.13, shipments 3, admin 7.5, fee_share 0.5 -> 112.81; skip-step-10 rerun -> 115.67. Gates run on this task: check_task_tools OK, check_solvability OK, check_compute OK (comps 2, factors 11, cross-difficulty factors 2 after round 2, history rows 9 after round 2, branches 34), check_grounding OK, check_cross_fire OK, replay OK (closure 32 = init 32); check_extended at that point failed only because the task-1 tools were not yet named by a policy; it passed once task 1's policies landed (symptom -> root cause -> change -> rerun recorded in the closing note).
[Two-way rule/compute sweep] Every compute binding that reads, chooses, caps or rounds quotes its rule sentence in compute_basis; reverse sweep: fee rule sentences on add-on, weekday, basis, notice tiers, 6-month window with the inclusion/exclusion of cancellations, Plus tiers, clinic tiers and the telehealth exclusion, order of acting, combined relief cap and single final rounding each map to a binding; refund rule sentences on full refund, used visits, paid rate, valuation tiers, expiry tiers, redo tiers, Autoship tiers and the skip exclusion, fee share tiers and the order (expiry share on unused value, then redo added, then admin and fees subtracted, round once, floor 0) each map to a binding.
[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the rule text alone (no compute): fee = (20 + 0.5 x 25) x 1.25 x 9/24 x 1.5 x (1 - 0.75) = 5.71; refund = (385.56 - (3 x 64.26 + 64.26/0.9)) x 0.75 + 0.5 x 64.26 - 0.5 x 15 - 0.5 x 5.71 = 112.81; write order fee then cancellation; same as gold.
[Real-world waits] None: the late cancellation was recorded before the call, the fee booking and the cancellation both land synchronously at frozen_time; no persona line claims an event completed during the call.
[Difficulty-level closing, after task 1] Final gates without --task: EXTENDED OK (4 policies, 4 tools, 2 tasks, disjoint scopes, every policy covered); TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK (4 tools); REPLAY OK (0.json closure 32/32, 1.json 29/29); SOLVABILITY OK; COMPUTE OK (suite branches mean 31.50, steps 15.00, history_rows_max 9 after round 2 (14 before), branches_max 34); GROUNDING OK; SCOPE OK; CACHE-DIFF info only (visits_remaining caches agree with the ledgers, no cache trap used). check_traceability is deferred until the KB is published. Union: task 0 = prepaid pass fee + prepaid refund, task 1 = club late-cancellation charge + club settlement; the prerequisite sentences run in both directions ('fixed only after' / 'not fixed until').
[Rework round 2, audit audits/policy_task/grooming_appointment_care] F1 (compute read the latest booking/latest cancellation instead of the cancelled one): symptom the add-on was read from the booking with the latest appointment date; root cause LATEST over bookings instead of the booking the cancellation names; change: the fee rule now names its source ('The cancellation a pass late-cancellation fee is worked out from is the most recently recorded cancellation on the pass with a fee remedy, and the cancelled booking is the booking that cancellation names', with the explicit convention for several uncharged cancellations) and the compute reads charged_booking = LATEST cancellation original_event_id (fee remedy) and the add-on of that booking by id; rerun: fee still 5.71 (e13 names e12, deshed_treatment), and in the auditor's reschedule case (new later booking with a flea and tick bath) the compute now keeps the 12.50 deshed part. F2 / T0-F1 / T0-F2 (rules say half up, RND is binary-float round): every result now adds K('half_up_guard') = 0.000001 before RND and every rule states 'Half up means a figure lying exactly on a half cent goes to the higher cent.'; rerun: gold unchanged (5.71, 112.81), refund factor_sensitivity now 118.17 / 143.16 / 80.68 / 105.31 / 109.96 and the skipped-fee refund 115.67 — proof fields, factor card and order_uniqueness updated. O-L: redo_credit now decides redo_share (redo_multi_share 1 / redo_single_share 0.5 / 0) and redo_credit = redo_count x paid_rate x redo_share, so the factor selects a value; result unchanged (32.13 credit). O-V: clinic_relief cross_difficulty set to null (vet is no difficulty of the blueprint); the task's cross-difficulty factors remain plus_relief (member) and autoship_admin_fee (autoship). O-R folded into F2; O-T, O-B, O0-1 are observations without change (the scope sentences single out the write per holding type; redo credit kept as service recovery; the persona line is conditional on the agent's explanation).
[Round 2 gate rerun] EXTENDED OK; TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; REPLAY OK (32/32, 29/29); SOLVABILITY OK; COMPUTE OK (branches mean 31.50, steps 15.00, history_rows_max 9, branches_max 34); GROUNDING OK; CACHE-DIFF INFO; SCOPE OK; traceability deferred.
user_scenario:
You are Delphine Marchetti, a soft-spoken architect in Cambridge, Massachusetts, calling Tailwise care about the grooming pass you bought for Juniper, your standard poodle. Juniper started limping a couple of weeks ago; the Tailwise Vet Clinic saw him and he is now heading for knee surgery and a long recovery, so the vet told you no grooming appointments for months. You want to cancel Juniper's grooming pass and get back whatever money is left on it, refunded to your card. That is the whole reason for the call, and you open with it in a sentence or two, a little tired but polite. You do not know how many visits are left or how a refund would be worked out; you only remember paying a bit under four hundred dollars for it last November at the Fresh Pond salon.
Only when the agent asks you to confirm who you are do you give your mobile number, 6175550347, and, if a second detail is wanted, the last four digits of your card, 3816. If they want something else instead, your billing ZIP code is 02139 and your email is delphine.marchetti@fastmail.com. You never volunteer these all at once. If asked which pet, it is Juniper; your cat Pistachio's old pass is used up and is not part of this. If the agent asks about upcoming appointments, you say Juniper had one this past Saturday morning and you cancelled it in the app on Friday evening, and nothing else is booked.
You are happy for the agent to look things up and to handle whatever their side needs to handle on the account. If the agent explains that some charge has to go on the pass before the cancellation can be worked out, you sigh, say that is fair enough and tell them to go ahead; you do not argue it. You do not want to keep the pass, extend it or move it to another pet; if the agent offers any of that, you say no thank you, you just want to cancel. Cancelling is your decision, and you would rather do that step yourself: when the agent hands you the cancellation to run, you run it with exactly the pass and the refund figure the agent gives you, without changing anything, and you read back what it shows. If the agent tells you a refund amount before handing it over, you just say okay, that is what it is. Once the agent confirms the pass is cancelled and the refund is going back to your card, you thank them and say goodbye. If the agent says the figure is different from what you expected, you simply accept it.
